title: Per-Object Velocity Motion Blur
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN importmap for three, three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader, three/addons/postprocessing/EffectComposer, three/addons/postprocessing/RenderPass, three/addons/postprocessing/ShaderPass) that implements per-object velocity-based motion blur as a post-processing effect.

SCENE SETUP:
- Create a WebGLRenderer with antialias, size 1024x768, appended to document.body with id='canvas-container'.
- Background color #111122.
- PerspectiveCamera at (0, 2, 8) looking at origin.
- Add a HemisphereLight(0xffffff, 0x444444, 1.5) and a DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 1.0) at (5, 10, 5).
- Create a ground plane (PlaneGeometry 20x20, MeshStandardMaterial gray #555555) rotated -PI/2 on X.
- Load 'Michelle.glb' using GLTFLoader. Once loaded, scale the model to height ~1.5 units. Place it at position (0, 0, 0). Play the first AnimationClip from the GLTF if available using an AnimationMixer.
- Create 3 additional simple moving objects: a red sphere (radius 0.3) orbiting the scene at radius 3 and height 1.5, a blue cube (size 0.4) bouncing up and down at x=-2 between y=0.4 and y=3, and a green torus (0.3, 0.1) moving linearly back and forth along z from -4 to 4 at x=2, y=1.

VELOCITY MOTION BLUR SYSTEM:
- Implement a custom velocity buffer pass. For each moving object, track its previous world position each frame. Compute a screen-space velocity vector = (currentScreenPos - previousScreenPos).
- Store velocity data per object in an array.
- Create a custom ShaderPass that uses these velocity vectors to blur pixels along the velocity direction. The blur is applied as a full-screen post-process. The blur samples along the velocity direction (use 8 samples). The blur intensity is controlled by a uniform 'uBlurStrength' (default 1.0, range 0.0 to 3.0).
- Use EffectComposer with: RenderPass -> custom VelocityBlurPass.

INTERACTION & CONTROLS:
- A slider (id='blur-strength-slider', min=0, max=3, step=0.1, default=1.0) with a label (id='blur-strength-label') showing 'Blur Strength: 1.0'.
- A checkbox (id='blur-toggle', checked by default) to enable/disable the motion blur pass entirely. Label: 'Motion Blur'.
- A dropdown (id='speed-select') with options: 'Slow' (value=0.5), 'Normal' (value=1.0, default selected), 'Fast' (value=2.0), 'Extreme' (value=4.0). This multiplies the animation speed of ALL moving objects and the AnimationMixer timeScale.
- A button (id='pause-btn') that toggles pause/resume of all motion. Text toggles between 'Pause' and 'Resume'.
- A button (id='reset-btn') that resets all objects to their initial positions, speed to Normal, blur strength to 1.0, blur enabled, and unpauses.
- Keyboard: press 'B' to toggle motion blur on/off (same as checkbox). Press 'Space' to toggle pause (same as pause button).
- Style the HUD controls in a panel at top-left, semi-transparent dark background, white text, z-index 1000.

STATE MANAGEMENT:
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame with:
- blurEnabled: boolean
- blurStrength: number (the uniform value)
- speedMultiplier: number (current speed factor)
- paused: boolean
- elapsedTime: number (total unpaused elapsed time in seconds)
- spherePosition: {x, y, z} (red sphere world position)
- cubePosition: {x, y, z} (blue cube world position)
- torusPosition: {x, y, z} (green torus world position)
- michelleLoaded: boolean
- sphereVelocityMagnitude: number (screen-space velocity magnitude of sphere)
- cubeVelocityMagnitude: number (screen-space velocity magnitude of cube)
- torusVelocityMagnitude: number (screen-space velocity magnitude of torus)
- composerPassCount: number (number of passes in EffectComposer)
- frameCount: number (incremented each rendered frame)
- objectCount: number (total mesh count in scene)
- mixerTimeScale: number (AnimationMixer.timeScale)
- blurSamples: number (number of blur samples, should be 8)
physics_constraints: Sphere orbits at constant radius 3 in XZ plane at y=1.5. Cube bounces between y=0.4 and y=3 (sinusoidal). Torus moves linearly along z between -4 and 4 at constant x=2, y=1. Velocity magnitudes must be non-negative and NaN-free. When paused, all positions freeze and velocities drop to 0. Speed multiplier scales all motion uniformly.
